name: tag_create_unique_per_space
description: #5236 / #5237 — a tag NAME is unique per space at creation, and the tags cache keeps one row per space. The harness space seeds a `todo` tag (`S2`); a seed id is zero-padded, so it sorts below every minted ULID and is the row the old vault-wide `UNIQUE (name)` kept. The ops create a second space (`C1`) and run `create_block` with `blockType: tag` into it, as the IPC runs it (`via: command`, so the RETURN is the record): `todo` is a NEW tag (`C2`) because uniqueness is per space, and before 0121 it was exactly the tag the cache could not hold — the smaller-id `todo` in the harness space owned the slot, so `Work`'s Tags view, its filters and its `tag:#` search never saw it (#5237). Then `Todo` into the same space: a case variant, the identity `normalize_tag_name` folds, answers the SAME label and no second block (#5236: the header's "Create" and the `#name` input rule each trust their own picker cache, and only the backend sees both). The reads: the unscoped prefix list carries BOTH `todo` rows — under the old constraint it carried one — and the harness space's own listing names only ITS `todo`. A query step cannot name an op-created space (`expand_query_args` knows `$SPACE` and `S<n>`), so `Work`'s listing is pinned by its cache row in the prefix list, not by `list_all_tags_in_space`.

ops.comment: The second space. Its `todo` below gets a minted ULID, larger than the seeded `S2`: under the old vault-wide UNIQUE it was the loser, the tag its own space could not list.
ops.name: a_second_space

ops.comment: The same name as the harness space's seeded tag, in ANOTHER space: a second tag — a new block, top-level (manually created tags have no parent), stamped into `C1` — because uniqueness is per space.
ops.name: the_same_name_in_another_space_is_a_new_tag

ops.comment: The same name in the same space, as a case variant: `normalize_tag_name` folds it, so this resolves to the tag above — same label, the EXISTING spelling (`todo`), no new block in the snapshot, no op in the digest. A stack that minted a second tag answers a new label here.
ops.name: a_case_variant_resolves_to_the_existing_tag

queries.comment: The unscoped prefix scan carries BOTH spaces' `todo` rows: one per space, neither evicting the other. Under the pre-0121 cache the `Work` row could not exist — `UNIQUE (name)` was held by the smaller-id seeded tag.
queries.name: the_prefix_list_carries_one_todo_per_space
queries.unordered: two byte-identical names: `ORDER BY name` leaves their relative order to the tie-break between a seed id and a minted one

queries.comment: The harness space lists its OWN `todo` and not `Work`'s: the listing is scoped by the tag block's space, and the cache row it reads is the per-space one.
queries.name: the_harness_space_lists_only_its_own_todo
